heard: A star 12 miles wide, physically warped Earth's atmosphere. The Magnetar SGR 180620 is a dead star with a magnetic field of 1,000 trillion gauss. On December 27, 2004, on the opposite side of the Milky Way, magnetic stress fractured its ultra-dense core in a massive star quake. In a tenth of a second, the rupture released more energy than the sun does in 150,000 years. Traveling 50,000 light years, the burst momentarily matched the full moon's brightness in gamma rays. That wave struck our ionosphere, ionizing gas and forcing the upper atmosphere to expand. If this erupted within 10 light years, it would have caused mass extinction. Even from across the galaxy, this tiny starquake still physically warped the world above us.
